loco.title: The Locomotive
loco.headline: The piston turns the wheel by a crank, not a gear.
loco.body: Steam pushes the piston back and forth inside the cylinder; the connecting rod turns each stroke into one turn of the driving wheel. Turner's engine is generally identified as a Firefly-class locomotive, per the National Gallery, with a single pair of 7 ft driving wheels. At 60 mph that wheel turns about 240 times a minute. Move the lever to change the speed.
loco.source: Source: The National Gallery, NG538 entry; Grace's Guide, GWR Firefly class.
loco.closing: This is a reading of the painting, not a record of the machine.

bridge.title: The Viaduct
bridge.headline: Brunel's brick arches at Maidenhead were the flattest in Britain.
bridge.body: Two 128 ft spans rise only 24 ft 3 in. The directors made Brunel leave the wooden centering in place; he eased it, an autumn storm in 1839 blew it down, and the arches stood. Push the rise up toward a semicircle and the line of thrust leaves the ring at the haunch; bring it back down and the ring holds. Slide the span and rise, then export the arch.
bridge.source: Source: Maidenhead Railway Bridge records; J. Heyman, The Masonry Arch, 1982.
bridge.closing: This is a reading of the painting, not a record of the bridge.

hare.title: The Hare
hare.headline: Turner painted the hare about the size of a thumbnail.
hare.body: A hare runs along the track ahead of the engine, almost invisible at viewing distance. It is usually read as Turner's comment on speed: the fastest animal in the English countryside against the new machine. This view is the untouched original at full resolution, not a reconstruction.
hare.source: Source: The National Gallery, NG538 entry.
hare.closing: This is a reading of the painting, not a record of the animal.
